steps.say: Bladder pain syndrome is defined by time and exclusion. It means pelvic pain or pressure felt to come from the bladder, with urinary symptoms lasting over six weeks and no infection found. Pain plus duration points here, while urgency alone points elsewhere.
steps.tx: **IC/BPS** (interstitial cystitis or bladder pain syndrome) is **chronic pelvic pain** (pelvic pain, pressure, or discomfort perceived from the bladder) with lower urinary tract symptoms for over **6 weeks** (six weeks) without infection. The definition matters: urgency and frequency alone point elsewhere, while pain plus duration points to the bladder wall itself.

rows: Chronic pelvic pain, pressure, or discomfort from bladder
No infection to explain the picture
Urgency alone without pain points elsewhere

steps.say: Hunner lesions identify the ulcer subtype. They are found in five to ten in a hundred patients as red patches with radiating vessels that tear and bleed when the bladder is stretched with fluid. Finding one changes treatment completely, because burning or steroid injection of the patch brings rapid relief.
steps.tx: **Hunner lesions** (Hunner ulcers, inflammatory bladder patches) appear in **5% to 10%** (five to ten in a hundred) of patients at cystoscopy as circumscribed erythematous areas with **radiating capillaries** (spoke-like vessels) that tear and bleed with **hydrodistension** (fluid stretching of the bladder). Finding one changes management, because lesion-directed fulguration or steroid injection brings rapid relief that diffuse disease rarely achieves.

vis.alt: Bladder view with Hunner lesion, glomerulations, barrier defect, and mast cells.
vis.caption: Hunner lesion with glomerulations and barrier defect at cystoscopy. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Glomerulations do not make the diagnosis. These pinpoint bleeds appear after gentle bladder stretching but healthy bladders and overactive bladder have them too. They are non-specific and no longer required, so a bladder full of them without pain history fails to confirm the disease.
steps.tx: **Glomerulations** (petechial submucosal bleeds after **hydrodistension**) are non-specific and no longer considered mandatory or pathognomonic for IC/BPS. They occur in healthy bladders and overactive bladder too, so a bladder full of glomerulations without the pain history fails to confirm disease, and their absence never excludes it.

rows: None: seen in healthy and overactive bladders

steps.say: The barrier theory explains the pain. When the protective sugar coating of the bladder lining breaks, urinary potassium seeps into the wall where it excites pain fibres and mast cells. Every fill soaks exposed nerve endings in potassium rich urine, which explains pain with filling and relief after voiding.
steps.tx: Disruption of the protective urothelial **glycosaminoglycan** layer (the **GAG layer**, sugar coating of the lining) lets urinary solutes, especially potassium, penetrate the submucosa, activating sensory C-fibers and **mast cells** (inflammatory allergy cells). Every fill soaks exposed endings in potassium-rich urine, which explains pain with filling and relief after voiding.

rows: Sensory C-fibers and mast cells fire
Pain with filling, relief with voiding

steps.say: One oral drug repairs the barrier specifically. Pentosan polysulfate sodium in a dose of one hundred milligrams three times daily remains the only approved oral drug for the disease itself, and it works by replenishing the sugar coating. Long use needs eye checks because silent retinal damage can threaten vision.
steps.tx: **Pentosan polysulfate sodium** (barrier-replenishing oral drug, **Elmiron**) **100 mg three times daily** (one hundred milligrams) is the only oral FDA-approved disease-specific drug; it replenishes the glycosaminoglycan coating. Long-term use requires baseline and periodic ophthalmologic screening because **pigmentary maculopathy** (retinal pigment damage) can develop silently and threaten vision.

rows: Baseline and periodic eye screening for maculopathy

steps.say: Pain modulation comes from an antidepressant. Amitriptyline twenty five to seventy five milligrams at night relieves urgency, frequency, and night voiding together through several nerve calming actions. Sleepiness forbids daytime dosing, so the whole dose is taken at night, and benefit builds over weeks.
steps.tx: **Amitriptyline** (tricyclic antidepressant) **25 to 75 mg nightly** (twenty five to seventy five milligrams) relieves symptoms via anticholinergic, antihistaminic, and central **neuropathic pain modulation** (brain-level pain dampening) pathways. Sedation confines dosing to night-time, and benefit builds over weeks rather than days, helping urgency, frequency, and nocturia together.

steps.say: Ulcer disease is burned or injected directly. Burning the patch with electric current or laser, or injecting steroid beneath it, produces rapid and deep remission in ulcer type disease. The effect outlasts tablets because the diseased patch itself is destroyed, though new patches elsewhere need repeat treatment.
steps.tx: Endoscopic **Hunner fulguration** (lesion burning) by electrocautery or laser ablation, or **triamcinolone injection** (steroid placed into submucosa) directly into Hunner lesions, provides rapid, profound remission in ulcer-type IC/BPS. Destroying the diseased patch outlasts systemic drugs, though new lesions elsewhere need repeat treatment.

rows: Electrocautery or laser ablation of the patch
Rapid, profound remission in ulcer-type disease

steps.say: Bladder wash treatments act on the surface repeatedly. Dimethyl sulfoxide, heparin, lidocaine, and hyaluronate are run into the bladder through a catheter and held there, where they rebuild the barrier and calm nerve inflammation. The numbing drug gives quick but brief relief that confirms the bladder as the pain source.
steps.tx: **Intravesical therapy** (bladder instillation treatment) with **DMSO** (dimethyl sulfoxide), **heparin instillation** (blood-thinner coating), lidocaine, and sodium hyaluronate restores the urothelial barrier and quiets C-fiber inflammation. Lidocaine brings quick brief numbness that proves the bladder generates the pain, while heparin and hyaluronate restore protection across courses of weeks.
